notes: Birds of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands that a visitor can realistically find: Port Blair and Chidiya Tapu, Mount Harriet and Wandoor, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep), Baratang and the North and Middle Andaman forests, plus the boat trips to Ross, North Bay and the outer reefs. The database lists these birds under India, so the pack is hand-picked from India's species that the country trip does not hold, ranked with GBIF/eBird record counts (occurrence.csv, whole India, so for the endemics it is the Andamans alone) and birding knowledge. It holds 19 Andaman endemics and endemic-status birds (Andaman Woodpecker, Andaman Drongo, Andaman Coucal, Andaman Crake, Andaman Masked-Owl, Andaman Scops Owl, Andaman Boobook, Andaman Woodpigeon, Andaman Green-Pigeon, Andaman Cuckoo-Dove, Andaman Bulbul, Andaman Treepie, Andaman Shama, Andaman Flowerpecker, Andaman Serpent-Eagle, Andaman Teal, Andaman Cuckooshrike, Andaman Nightjar and White-headed Starling), the island forms of widespread Asian birds that are only reliable here (Long-tailed and Red-breasted Parakeet, Vernal Hanging-Parrot, Pied and Green Imperial-Pigeon, Ruddy and Collared Kingfisher, Dollarbird, Violet Cuckoo, Black-naped Monarch, Mangrove Whistler, Ornate Sunbird, Pacific Swallow, Asian Glossy Starling, Common Hill Myna), and the sea and shore birds of the coast and the ferries (White-bellied Sea-Eagle, Pacific Reef-Heron, Beach Thick-knee, frigatebirds, boobies, tropicbirds, terns and a noddy, and the waders of the beaches). Left out on purpose: the Nicobar birds (Nicobar Pigeon, Nicobar Megapode, Nicobar Sparrowhawk, Nicobar Bulbul, Nicobar Parakeet, Nicobar Imperial-Pigeon, Nicobar Serpent-Eagle, Nicobar Scops Owl, Nicobar Jungle Flycatcher and Nicobar Hooded Pitta), because the Nicobars are closed to ordinary visitors, and Narcondam Hornbill, because Narcondam is closed too. Walden's Hornbill does not occur here. Vagrants and expedition-only seabirds were not considered. Common birds the country trip already has (Brahminy Kite, Asian Koel, Greater Flameback, Blue-tailed Bee-eater, Oriental Magpie-Robin, Common Iora and so on) are not repeated, and the Crab-Plover and Western Reef-Heron stay with the Gujarat pack. Because the pack was written alongside the other India packs, a few widespread birds (Common Hill Myna, Vernal Hanging-Parrot, Red-breasted Parakeet, Pacific Golden Plover, Eurasian Whimbrel, Bar-tailed Godwit, Terek Sandpiper, Greater Sand-Plover, Great Knot, Ruddy Turnstone) are kept here although another pack may claim them; settle any duplicate centrally. Left out for lack of usable or trustworthy photos in the library: Little Heron (no photos), Plume-toed Swiftlet and White-nest (Edible-nest) Swiftlet (only distant flight shots, colonies and nests, which cannot be identified), Roseate Tern (mixed with Common Tern), Sooty Tern (mixed with Bridled Tern), Cinnamon Bittern and Yellow Bittern (hidden in reeds, mixed with other bitterns). Shaky photo picks, to check on /trip-photos: Andaman Teal, Andaman Woodpigeon, Andaman Green-Pigeon, Andaman Cuckoo-Dove, Andaman Bulbul, Andaman Shama, Andaman Drongo, Great and Lesser Frigatebird (distant flight shots only, the species are hard to separate), Red-footed Booby, Black-naped Tern, Lesser Crested Tern, Pacific Swallow, Asian Glossy Starling, Mangrove Whistler, Collared Kingfisher, Pacific Golden Plover (American Golden Plover is a look-alike), Grey-tailed Tattler (Wandering Tattler is a look-alike), Greater Sand-Plover and Great Knot. 57 species.
